site.title: THREAD
site.question: How do culture, faith, family and stigma shape the way people in Malaysia test for, talk about and live with HIV?
site.lensLine: We look through a Malaysian lens: batik.
site.lens: Batik is made line by line. Wax drawn with a canting protects parts of the cloth from the dye and lets others take colour. We use that process to see what protects people, what marks them, and what is revealed once the wax comes off.

stages.text: Every cloth begins as a pattern. Culture, faith and family draw the lines people live within. We start by mapping them.
Wax protects whatever it touches. We look for what shields people from HIV stigma: care, trust and community.
Dye soaks into whatever is left open. Stigma settles the same way, quietly. We study where it lands.
Boiling lifts the wax away. We test what removes the barriers to testing, treatment and disclosure.
The finished cloth goes back to the community. At its centre, a red ribbon.

themes.name: People living with HIV
themes.short: Everyday life, wellbeing and care for people living with HIV in Malaysia.
themes.body:
We work alongside people living with HIV (PLHIV) to understand what helps them live well: disclosure, family and faith, stigma in health care and at work, mental health, and staying connected to care.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: Ageing with HIV
themes.short: Growing older with HIV, and the care and support that ageing brings.
themes.body:
More people with HIV are growing older thanks to effective treatment. We look at what ageing with HIV means in Malaysia: other health conditions, care needs, loneliness and support, and how services can keep up.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: Stigma & Discrimination
themes.short: Understanding stigma and discrimination in Malaysia, and finding ways to reduce it in health care and the community.

themes.name: Chemsex
themes.short: Sexualised drug use: experiences, harms, pleasure and support.
themes.body:
Chemsex is the use of drugs to enhance or prolong sex. We explore people's experiences of it, the risks for HIV, other infections and mental health, and what kinds of support people find acceptable.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: Sexual risk behaviour
themes.short: Sexual practices, testing and the choices people make about prevention.
themes.body:
We study how people think about sexual risk, testing and prevention, and how culture, relationships and stigma shape those choices.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: PrEP
themes.short: Pre-exposure prophylaxis: awareness, access, uptake and staying on it.
themes.body:
PrEP is medicine taken before possible exposure to prevent HIV. We look at who knows about it, who can get it, what makes people start or stop, and how stigma affects its use.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: Doxy-PEP
themes.short: Doxycycline after sex to prevent some bacterial STIs: views and use.
themes.body:
Doxy-PEP is the antibiotic doxycycline taken after sex to lower the chance of some bacterial sexually transmitted infections. We explore how acceptable it is, how people would use it, and concerns about resistance.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

themes.name: PEP
themes.short: Post-exposure prophylaxis: knowing about it and getting it in time.
themes.body:
PEP is a short course of HIV medicine started soon after a possible exposure, ideally within 72 hours. We look at awareness, the barriers to getting it quickly, and the experiences of people who seek it.

[Add what your team is focusing on in this theme.]

opps.title: Research Assistant
opps.summary: We are **open** to research assistants across our projects. [Hours and dates.] **Rolling applications, no deadline.**
opps.lede: Work alongside the research team on studies about HIV, culture and care in Malaysia. Hands-on research experience for students and recent graduates.
opps.l1:
Search for and screen research articles
Help prepare study materials and surveys
Support data collection, transcription and coding of interviews
Help with community engagement and outreach
Attend a weekly team meeting
opps.l2:
Training in qualitative and quantitative research methods
Experience in HIV and sexual health research
Your contribution named in publications, with co-authorship if you meet authorship criteria
A letter confirming your role and hours on completion
opps.l3:
Enrolled in or recently graduated from psychology, counselling, public health, social science or a related field
Comfortable reading academic papers in English
Respectful and non-judgemental when talking about HIV, sex and drug use
Careful with confidential information
Able to work independently and meet weekly targets
opps.l4:
Prior research experience
Familiarity with NVivo, SPSS, R or Excel
Experience with LGBTQ+ communities or people living with HIV
Speaks Bahasa Malaysia, Mandarin or Tamil
